notes: EBIT is proxied as consolidated operating income from the statement of income (not 'EBIT' explicitly disclosed). ([docs.aep.com](https://docs.aep.com/docs/investors/filings/docs/AEP_10K_2025.pdf))
Capex is proxied as 'Construction Expenditures' from investing activities; modeled as positive absolute values. ([docs.aep.com](https://docs.aep.com/docs/investors/filings/docs/AEP_10K_2025.pdf))

NWC definition (working-capital measure): (Total current assets - cash & cash equivalents - restricted cash - other temporary investments) - (Total current liabilities - short-term debt - long-term debt due within one year). This produces negative NWC for AEP in the historical period, consistent with utility working-capital structure. ([docs.aep.com](https://docs.aep.com/docs/investors/filings/docs/AEP_10K_2025.pdf))

Tax rate is modeled from historical effective tax rate but is materially affected by equity earnings, regulatory/timing items, and tax benefits; base-case tax_rate is therefore a simplified normalized assumption. ([docs.aep.com](https://docs.aep.com/docs/investors/filings/docs/AEP_10K_2025.pdf))
WACC is not explicitly provided in the sourced filings used here; it is set as an estimated base-case value for modeling continuity (scenarios adjust modestly).

NOL balance is taken from a deferred tax item ('Net Operating Loss Carryforward' line item) and may reflect the tax-effected value rather than the underlying gross NOL; NOL utilization percent is left null because the exact utilization schedule for the modeled NOL balance is not cleanly extractable from the cited excerpt. ([docs.aep.com](https://docs.aep.com/docs/investors/filings/docs/AEP_10K_2025.pdf))

catalysts: Progress and timing of transmission and other regulated investments receiving rate recovery (regulatory filings, approvals, and true-ups).

Execution of the contracted load growth pathway (incremental contracted load of 56 GW by 2030) supporting cash-flow durability. ([docs.aep.com](https://docs.aep.com/docs/newsroom/resources/earnings/2026-02/4Q25EarningsReleasePresentation.pdf))
Interest rate/credit spread environment impacting financing costs and regulatory capitalization rates for capital-heavy periods.
company_overview: AEP is one of the largest U.S. investor-owned electric utility holding companies, serving more than five million retail customers with vertically integrated and transmission/distribution operations. ([docs.aep.com](https://docs.aep.com/docs/investors/filings/docs/AEP_10K_2024.pdf))

2025 financials show total revenues of $21.876B and operating income (EBIT proxy) of $5.319B, with depreciation and amortization of $3.380B. ([docs.aep.com](https://docs.aep.com/docs/investors/filings/docs/AEP_10K_2025.pdf))

Strategic focus on system reliability and transmission buildout tied to contracted load growth (data centers and industrial demand). ([docs.aep.com](https://docs.aep.com/docs/newsroom/resources/earnings/2026-02/4Q25EarningsReleasePresentation.pdf))
current_context: AEP’s 4Q25 earnings release presentation guided 2026 operating EPS to $6.15-$6.45 and referenced 2026 capital investment of >$12B. ([docs.aep.com](https://docs.aep.com/docs/newsroom/resources/earnings/2026-02/4Q25EarningsReleasePresentation.pdf))

Management reiterated a 2026-2030 $72B capital plan, targeting ~10% rate base CAGR and 7%-9% operating EPS growth through 2030. ([docs.aep.com](https://docs.aep.com/docs/newsroom/resources/earnings/2026-02/4Q25EarningsReleasePresentation.pdf))

The presentation highlights incremental contracted load of 56 GW by 2030 and expects significant infrastructure investment from the high-growth transmission business. ([docs.aep.com](https://docs.aep.com/docs/newsroom/resources/earnings/2026-02/4Q25EarningsReleasePresentation.pdf))
investment_highlights: Base-case revenue growth of ~3-4% embeds rate-base expansion and load additions consistent with the 2026-2030 capital program and the guided operating earnings growth outlook. ([docs.aep.com](https://docs.aep.com/docs/newsroom/resources/earnings/2026-02/4Q25EarningsReleasePresentation.pdf))
EBIT margin is modeled to normalize from the 2025 elevated level toward ~0.22 by 2030 (operating-income proxy). ([docs.aep.com](https://docs.aep.com/docs/investors/filings/docs/AEP_10K_2025.pdf))

Sustained reinvestment: base-case capex intensity is held near the historical construction-expenditure-to-revenue range (~0.39x). ([docs.aep.com](https://docs.aep.com/docs/investors/filings/docs/AEP_10K_2025.pdf))

Working capital modeled as persistently negative but gradually improving vs the 2025 spike, reflecting utility working-capital dynamics from year to year. ([docs.aep.com](https://docs.aep.com/docs/investors/filings/docs/AEP_10K_2025.pdf))
key_risks: Regulatory lag or disallowances reducing allowed returns or slowing recovery of construction and operating costs.
Higher-than-modeled financing costs and lower equity/debt availability during the capital-intensive 2026-2030 window.
Adverse weather and fuel/power market volatility affecting earnings and cash flows despite regulatory mechanisms.
Nuclear and other environmental/compliance cost uncertainty affecting long-run cash needs.
